# FIXTURES-RANGES.md — libphext 0.6.1 range conformance fixtures: format spec

Shared conformance fixture set for the libphext ports → v0.6.1 program
(task 37.12.8/15.9.18/8.10.14). Extends the 0.6 chain fixture set
(FIXTURES.md, same directory). Every port consumes this set to prove its
v0.6.1 addressing layer matches the reference implementation exactly.

- **Reference:** libphext-rs 0.6.1 — tag `v0.6.1` (exo merge 65cc4798),
  PR https://github.com/wbic16/libphext-rs/pull/13.
- **Spec:** RANGE-SYNTAX-PROPOSAL.md (ratified by Will, 2026-11-15), same
  workspace directory.
- **Provenance:** every expected value was *generated by calling the
  reference library itself* (`parse_point_address`, `parse_range_address`,
  `Chain::resolve_point`, `Chain::resolve_range`, `Chain::fetch_point`,
  `Chain::fetch_range`) from a Rust harness (`gen-ranges`, run on
  aletheia-core, 2026-11-15). No expectation was hand-computed. The harness
  asserted canonical round-trips at generation time and, for every resolved
  range fetch, that the fragment parses back and every segment fetches back
  byte-identically from the fragment.
- **Canonical home in the rs repo:** `tests/fixtures/ranges/` on exo, where
  `tests/range_fixtures.rs` consumes the set. This workspace copy at
  `~/workspace/libphext-ports-v06/fixtures/ranges/` is a byte copy of the
  repo copy.

## File layout

```
fixtures/ranges/
  manifest.json        <- global manifest: format id, reference, all cases inline
  cases.tsv            <- index: "case<TAB><case>/input.phext" per line, header first
  <case>/
    input.phext        <- the exact input byte stream (a chain stream; use chain 0)
    manifest.json      <- per-case manifest (same schema as one entry of the global manifest)
    expected.tsv       <- line-oriented digest of the manifest for harnesses without JSON
    results/
      NN.txt           <- expected result bytes of the fetch op with index NN (empty file = empty result)
```

All inputs are valid UTF-8. Compare as bytes wherever your language allows
it. **Never** apply newline translation, trimming, or Unicode normalization.

## Op kinds

Each case carries an ordered op list. Ops apply to chain 0 of
`parse_chains(input)`.

| kind | input | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `parse_point` | a point address string | `canonical` (the canonical serialization) or `expected_error: true` |
| `parse_range` | a range address string | `canonical` or `expected_error: true` |
| `resolve_point` | a point address string (guaranteed to parse) | `resolve` = `"<universe>\|<coordinate>\|<char offset>"` or `expected_error: true` |
| `fetch_point` | a point address string | result bytes in `results/NN.txt`, plus `resolved` (whether resolve_point succeeds) |
| `fetch_range` | a range address string | result bytes in `results/NN.txt`, plus `resolved` (whether resolve_range succeeds) |

For fetch ops, `resolved=false` means resolution must fail in your port
*and* the fetch must return the recorded bytes (always empty) — the two
empty-result situations (resolved-but-empty vs unresolved) must stay
distinguishable in your implementation, exactly as in the reference.

`expected.tsv` carries the same data, one line per op, TAB-separated:

```
op	parse_point	<input>	canonical=<canonical or ->	error=<true|false>
op	parse_range	<input>	canonical=<canonical or ->	error=<true|false>
op	resolve_point	<input>	resolve=<u|coord|offset or ->	error=<true|false>
op	fetch_point	<input>	file=results/NN.txt	resolved=<true|false>
op	fetch_range	<input>	file=results/NN.txt	resolved=<true|false>
```

## Exact semantics the fixtures pin down (from the reference)

- **Grammar.** Point: `[$N:]<9D coordinate>[@<line>,<column>[+<offsetChars>]]`.
  Range: two points joined by exactly one hyphen. Unsigned decimal integers
  only — no signs, no whitespace, ever. Universe, coordinate components,
  line, and column are all ≥ 1. `+offset` may be 0. Range endpoints may not
  carry `+offset`.
- **Canonical form.** Endpoints ascending by (universe, coordinate, line,
  column); `$1:` never written (accepted on input); integers in minimal
  decimal form (leading zeros parse by value); no whitespace. A reversed
  range parses and normalizes — direction is discarded.
- **Positions are caret boundaries, half-open.** Column 1 is the boundary
  before a line's first character; a line of *n* characters has valid
  columns 1..*n*+1. Lines split on 0x0A (kept inside the scroll). Columns
  and offsets count **Unicode scalar values**, never bytes.
- **Endpoint roles.** An endpoint without `@`: as start = its scroll's
  first boundary; as end = its scroll's last boundary (whole scroll).
- **Scroll presence** is the phokenize sense used by the 0.6 fixtures: a
  coordinate is present exactly when the member's phokenize enumeration
  contains it. A range endpoint naming an absent scroll is a resolution
  error.
- **Resolution errors, never clamp.** Line past the scroll's last line,
  column past line length + 1, universe past the chain's length, absent
  endpoint scroll → resolution fails (fetch returns ""). No clamping, no
  panics.
- **Offset form.** From the point, forward N scalars within the scroll,
  terminating at the scroll boundary (clipped at the scroll's end). A point
  without `+offset` is a caret and fetches "".
- **Range fetch = a phext (chain) fragment.** The spanned text with
  structure bytes preserved: covered segments re-assembled at their
  coordinates (the reference builds each covered universe's fragment by
  inserting its non-empty segments, in ascending coordinate order, into an
  empty phext; empty segments contribute nothing), universes joined by
  CHAIN_BREAK (0x02), and **no trailing CHAIN_CLOSE** — a fragment is an
  excerpt, not a terminated chain. Scrolls strictly between the endpoints
  contribute whole segments; endpoint scrolls contribute partial segments.
  An empty range (start = end) fetches "".

## Case inventory (6 cases, 69 ops)

| Case | Ops | What it pins down |
|---|---|---|
| point-basics | 24 | Point parsing/canonical form, 10 parse rejections, resolution offsets incl. edge boundaries (last column of a line, scroll end), missing scroll/universe |
| offset-form | 12 | `+offsetChars`: scalar counting over multi-byte text, crossing line boundaries, clipping at the scroll end, `+0`, `$1:` input, caret point, resolution failures |
| range-within-scroll | 12 | The worked examples (span = chars 5–8 style half-open, whole line incl. newline, whole scroll, empty caret), reversed input, offset-endpoint rejection, out-of-range errors |
| range-cross-scroll | 6 | Partial + whole segments across scrolls and a section boundary, `@`-less whole-scroll endpoints, mixed granularity, missing endpoint scroll |
| range-multiverse | 8 | A closed 3-member chain: multiversal range (middle universe whole), range inside universe 2, whole-universe `@`-less range, canonical `$1:` drop, universe-past-end and missing-scroll errors |
| range-unicode | 7 | Emoji/CJK scrolls where byte and scalar offsets differ: resolution, offset fetch, and range fetches counted in scalars |
